answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when an audited task reveals duplicated identities coordinating to claim one reward. A timber supplier might bid at a wharf while a walnut broker bids elsewhere; if their commitments trace to the same controller, both risk losing collateral. Creating sybils therefore multiplies capital locked up and the losses from detection, rather than merely multiplying cheap accounts.
